title: Alternating cross slopes · level 2
description: Controlled saddle challenge with 60mm nominal local relief; identical geometry and material for both caster models.

route_region.definition: |x|<=1.8m and |y|<=2m, covering prescribed chassis routes and approximate wheel footprint.

slope_method: Grid-node finite differences, with separate exact triangle-face maximum; all exclude closing side walls. Whole-surface extrema include boundary blends.

parameters.level_changes: Height multiplier only; XY geometry, phases and contact settings stay fixed.
parameters.mechanism: Alternating cross-slope/camber and roll demand; phase offsets make the centerline exposure asymmetric without changing material properties.

figure.source: Derived from exact generated height grid; not a Gazebo camera image.

boundary_blend.note: Only outside the stress-route region is a flat probe/entry margin or boundary taper; no special flat road through the center.

terrain_friction.basis: Matches DART mesh attachment defaults; identical to prior validated shared terrain worlds. Runtime validation remains required.

smoke.scope: Short common centerline segment for pilot contact checks, not a full trajectory comparison or a guaranteed pass.

comparison_design.intended_paths: Reversals y±1.1; tight figure-eight x±.65,y±1; lateral turns x0..1.2,y−1.5..1.5; zigzag x±.6,y−1.5..1.5.
comparison_design.interpretation: Compare paired runs within terrain/level/route/seed. Do not select only conditions favoring either caster or call commanded-path yaw difference tire slip on a sloped turn.

research_sources.title: Kauzlarich, Bruning and Thacker: Wheelchair caster shimmy and turning resistance (1984)
research_sources.evidence: Experiments and equations distinguish caster shimmy and sliding-friction turning resistance; tire geometry changes both.
research_sources.limit: No critical shimmy speed or measured tire-loss coefficient is transferred to HAMR.

research_sources.title: Kauzlarich, Bruning and Thacker: Wheelchair caster shimmy II: damping (2000)
research_sources.evidence: The correction to the earlier shimmy analysis considers tire friction, spindle-bearing friction and hydraulic damping.
research_sources.limit: Rigid Coulomb contact and estimated joint damping do not reproduce calibrated tire-elastic shimmy.

research_sources.title: Sprigle, Huang and Misch: Measurement of rolling resistance and scrub torque of manual wheelchair drive wheels and casters (2022)
research_sources.evidence: Separate component tests measure coast-down rolling loss and loaded-wheel scrub torque; losses depend on load and surface and can trade off.
research_sources.limit: Local alignment, tracking and drive effort must be measured separately; one cannot infer real energy loss from yaw alignment alone.

research_sources.title: Development of wheelchair caster testing equipment and preliminary testing of caster models (2017)
research_sources.evidence: The apparatus tests square and 30-degree oblique slat impacts and reverses travel to exercise stem bearings. The preliminary study found no significant durability difference between impact angles.
research_sources.limit: Oblique excitation motivates a test condition, not a prediction of greater damage or a fatigue/standards-validation claim.

research_sources.title: Udengaard and Iagnemma: Analysis, Design, and Control of an Omnidirectional Mobile Robot in Rough Terrain (2009)
research_sources.evidence: The rough-terrain controller considers wheel-terrain contact angles in an active split-offset caster system.
research_sources.limit: The mechanism is active and differs from both passive HAMR models; this motivates terrain-normal-aware interpretation, not transferring performance claims.

limitations: Rigid analytic geometry; no soil deformation, loose gravel, fatigue or tire elasticity.
Estimated caster inertia, bearing loss and different wheel geometries remain model confounds.
Height levels are bounded engineering choices, not literature-derived pass/fail thresholds.
No guarantee either robot traverses until a physical pilot is run; no motor/climb capability claim.
Mesh colors encode altitude only and do not change material friction.

generator.randomness: none; analytic grid and fixed phases/pad centers
